evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: Maria Svolou ("née" Desypri; 1892 – 1976) was a Greek feminist and socialist leader.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: Maria Desypri was born around 1892 in Athens to George Desypros and his wife.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: Maria was one of four daughters and lived for two years in Piraeus.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: She moved with her family to Larissa in her youth when her father was appointed director of a branch of the Greek National Bank.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: There she studied at the Arsakeion School of Larissa, graduating around 1907.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: Following the death of her father in 1915, the family returned to Athens.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: She received a certificate in French Studies in 1916 and a license for teaching French from the Ecclesiastical and Public Education Ministries in 1919.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: Svolou was active in the women's movement of Greece from a young age.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: She married law professor Alexandros Svolos in 1923.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: As secretary of the League for Women's Rights she advocated for the creation of night schools for women who worked and fought against prostitution.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: She campaigned and wrote on behalf of equality for the women of Greece.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: She was inspector of labor for the Ministry of Economics and used her position there to draw attention the poor working and housing conditions of impoverished working women.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: Svolou was involved in liberal politics from 1911 to 1936 and supported the peace movement.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: She was editor of the magazine "Woman's Struggle" and was exiled from Greece from 1936 to 1940 with her husband by dictator Ioannis Metaxas.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: Svolou was a leader of the liberal feminist movement but believed that gender equality could only be attained after fundamental societal change.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: She returned to Greece in 1940 and volunteered in the Greco-Italian War as a nurse.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: She later organised meals with the Red Cross for children during the German occupation of Greece.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: Svolou joined the EAM-ELAS resistance movement and was elected a member of the National Council, while her husband became chairman of the EAM-led Political Committee of National Liberation.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: Svolou sympathised with the Communists and was exiled again in 1948, during the Greek Civil War.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: Following her return she ran for the Parliament as a member of the United Democratic Left.

evidence.title: Maria Svolou
evidence.text: She was elected twice and was a member of the party's Central Committee.
